title: util.SanitizeControlChars is the shared helper for stripping control chars + safe UTF-8 truncation
answers: How do I strip control characters and truncate a string safely in Grafana backend code?
What function avoids splitting a multi-byte rune when truncating a label/header value?
Is there an existing util for sanitizing untrusted strings before exposing them?
body:
util.SanitizeControlChars(s, maxBytes) in pkg/util/strings.go strips ASCII control chars (including CRLF, via strings.Map removing r<0x20 or 0x7f) and then truncates with util.TruncateUTF8 so the cut never splits a multi-byte rune. eval.sanitizeHeaderValue (pkg/services/ngalert/eval/eval.go) and schedule.sanitizePluginOriginLabel (pkg/services/ngalert/schedule/metrics.go) both now delegate to it instead of each reimplementing strings.Map.
Convention: new code needing to sanitize an untrusted string for a header, metric label, or similar exposed surface should call util.SanitizeControlChars rather than duplicating the strip/truncate logic.
Constraints: only valid for byte-length caps on UTF-8 text where exact truncation point doesn't matter semantically (labels, headers) — not for binary data.
applies: any Go backend code sanitizing untrusted/user-controlled strings before exposing as metric labels, headers, or similar
